hypotheses.title: Short-Tenor Option Open-Interest Breakeven Gamma Floor Distance (20d)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: The combined call and put breakeven price (option_breakeven_20) reflects the collective open-interest-weighted pivot price of option market participants expiring in 20 days. When spot price trades comfortably above this combined breakeven ((close - option_breakeven_20) / close > 0), market makers operate in positive gamma positioning, suppressing downside volatility and dampening inventory liquidations. Liquid volume decay prevents chasing temporary spikes.
confounders: Low overall option liquidity causing stale open-interest breakeven calculations
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if equities trading above option breakeven break through downside support during market corrections.

candidates.expression: group_rank((close - option_breakeven_20) / close, market) - group_rank(ts_decay_linear(volume / adv20, 5), market)

hypotheses.title: Intermediate-Tenor Option Open-Interest Breakeven Gamma Floor Distance (60d)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: 60-day combined option breakeven (option_breakeven_60) captures quarterly institutional positioning around earnings cycles. Equities trading at a substantial buffer above their 60-day open-interest breakeven floor have established durable institutional accumulation with minimal near-term gamma flip risk. Market-wide cross-sectional ranking ensures complete universe coverage with zero subindustry starvation.
confounders: Major quarterly earnings guidance reductions breaking established options pinning levels
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if quarterly breakeven support fails to protect against post-earnings drawdowns.

candidates.expression: group_rank((close - option_breakeven_60) / close, market) - group_rank(ts_decay_linear(volume / adv20, 5), market)

hypotheses.title: 60-Day Options Implied Volatility Skew Exhaustion Reversion
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Implied volatility skew measured as (implied_volatility_put_60 - implied_volatility_call_60) captures medium-term institutional tail-risk hedging demand. When panic buying pushes put implied volatility far above call IV, downside hedging costs become excessive. Equities with the lowest relative skew (-(implied_volatility_put_60 - implied_volatility_call_60)) exhibit strong institutional balance sheet confidence and outperform during relief rallies.
confounders: Fundamental credit degradation where elevated put skew accurately discounts credit rating downgrades
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if low-skew equities fail to outperform high-skew peers over 15-day holding horizons.

candidates.expression: group_rank(-(implied_volatility_put_60 - implied_volatility_call_60), market) - 0.25 * group_rank(ts_decay_linear((close - vwap) / close, 5), market)
